title: Transport of one signed Koszul summand
statement: For one selected index i in I in the model of [def-cbc-signed-koszul-completion-model], tensor the endomorphism (-1)^{card {j in I : j<i}} times (ringedKoszulScalar(a_i))^{m+1}, then the erased basis inclusion and its degree transport. After the total-tensor sign (-1)^{q+card I} and inclusion, the result equals the global-section coefficient action of (-1)^{q+card I}(-1)^{card {j in I : j<i}}a_i^{m+1}, followed by the coefficient-degree equality transport and erased summand inclusion.

proof.text: Identify the rank-one global-section multiplication map with the Hom scalar action on its identity. Use the naturality of tensorObjIsoSheafification and the module sheafification unit to prove that tensorLeft preserves the global-section scalar action: on a pure tensor this is x tensor (b f(y)) = b (x tensor f(y)). Compose with the inverse right unitor and use bilinearity of composition. This is proved directly, without an unproved scalar-transport lemma.

Global-section multiplication on the rank-one module is a ring map into its endomorphisms (checked sectionwise), so the integer sign (-1)^|{j in I:j<i}| times the (m+1)-st power of multiplication by a_i is multiplication by rho((-1)^|{j in I:j<i}| a_i^(m+1)). Substitute the two degree equalities in a generic tensor-inclusion transport identity; after substitution both sides coincide, by proof irrelevance. Apply the identity to the erased basis and combine the total-tensor unit sign with the signed scalar power. Split by parity of q+|I| and use rho preserving multiplication and negation.

theorem ringedNegativeKoszulSummand_D₂_term
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) {A : Type z} [CommRing A]
    (ρ : A →+* RingCat.sectionsSubring (O.obj ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat))
    (r : ℕ) (a : Fin (r + 1) → A) (m : ℕ) (K : ringedSiteComplex O) (q : ℤ)
    (I : Finset (Fin (r + 1))) (i : Fin (r + 1)) (hi : i ∈ I)
    (hdeg : q + (I.card : ℤ) = (q + 1) + ((I.erase i).card : ℤ))
    (hsrc : -(I.card : ℤ) + 1 = -((I.erase i).card : ℤ)) :
    letI : IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O)) :=
      SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian _
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory O
    letI := SheafOfModules.symmetricCategory O
    letI := Classical.choice (SheafOfModules.tensorClosed O).1
    letI := Classical.choice (SheafOfModules.tensorClosed O).2.1
    let Q := ringedNegativeKoszul O (r + 1)
      (fun j ↦ ⟨(ρ (a j)).val, (ρ (a j)).property⟩) m
    ((-1 : ℤˣ) ^ (q + (I.card : ℤ))) •
        (MonoidalCategory.rightUnitor (K.X (q + I.card))).inv ≫
      (MonoidalCategory.tensorLeft (K.X (q + I.card))).map
        (((-1 : ℤ) ^ (I.filter (fun j ↦ j < i)).card •
            (ringedKoszulScalar O ⟨(ρ (a i)).val, (ρ (a i)).property⟩) ^ (m + 1)) ≫
          ringedNegativeKoszulBasis O
            (r + 1) (fun j ↦ ⟨(ρ (a j)).val, (ρ (a j)).property⟩) m
            (I.erase i) (-((I.erase i).card : ℤ)) ≫
          eqToHom (congrArg Q.X hsrc.symm)) ≫
      CochainComplex.ιMapBifunctor K Q (MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor _)
        (q + I.card) (-(I.card : ℤ) + 1) (q + 1) (by omega) =
      ringedKoszulCoefficientSMul O ρ
          ((if Even (q + (I.card : ℤ)) then (1 : A) else -1) *
            (-1 : A) ^ (I.filter (fun j ↦ j < i)).card * a i ^ (m + 1))
        (K.XIsoOfEq hdeg).hom ≫
        (MonoidalCategory.rightUnitor (K.X (q + 1 + (I.erase i).card))).inv ≫
        (MonoidalCategory.tensorHom (𝟙 _) 
          (ringedNegativeKoszulBasis O
            (r + 1) (fun j ↦ ⟨(ρ (a j)).val, (ρ (a j)).property⟩) m
            (I.erase i) (-((I.erase i).card : ℤ)))) ≫
        CochainComplex.ιMapBifunctor K Q (MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor _)
          (q + 1 + (I.erase i).card) (-((I.erase i).card : ℤ)) (q + 1) (by omega)

statement_change.what: The left side used the unsigned first power of a_i although the right side used its signed (m+1)-st power. For one factor, m=1, a_0=2, K=O[0], q=-1 and I={0}, the old statement equates multiplication by 2 and 4. Insert the signed power on the left; the right side and all hypotheses stay unchanged.
